procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment dated 16.12.2019 passed by the Allahabad High Court in Application U/S 482 No. 41533/2019, which quashed criminal proceedings against the respondent.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The Allahabad High Court initially passed an order on 16.12.2019 quashing criminal proceedings. Later, a petition (number 41533 of 2019) was filed seeking to recall the 16.12.2019 order. This recall application was dismissed on 02.04.2024.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The victim, Rinki, wanted to file a Special Leave Petition (SLP) before the Supreme Court after the dismissal of the recall application by the High Court in April 2024. Criminal Appeal Nos. 3883-3884 of 2024 were filed. A complaint was also filed with the Secretary General of the Supreme Court of India on 9.7.2024. The appeals were ultimately disposed of by the Supreme Court.

directions: The same be listed for the submission of the Report by the CBI on 25th November, 2024.

issue.issue_text: Whether the High Court's judgment, which quashed the criminal proceedings against the respondent under Section 482 of the CrPC, should be upheld.

facts: An appeal was filed in the Supreme Court challenging a High Court judgment dated 16.12.2019.
The High Court's judgment had quashed criminal proceedings against respondent no. 2, Ajay Katara.
The appeal was filed in the name of the petitioner, Bhagwan Singh.
law: Filing false court proceedings in someone's name without their knowledge, consent, or authority, using fabricated documents, constitutes an abuse of the process of law and a fraud on the court.
application: Upon reviewing the case records, the Supreme Court discovered that the appeal proceedings were filed in the petitioner's name without his knowledge or consent.
The Court found that the proceedings relied on false and fabricated documents, including vakalatnamas and affidavits.
It concluded that this was a deliberate attempt by other respondents (nos. 3 and 4) and their advocates to falsely implicate respondent no. 2 and deceive both the High Court and the Supreme Court.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court did not rule on the merits of the High Court's decision to quash the criminal proceedings. Instead, it disposed of the appeals because they were found to be fraudulent and an abuse of the legal process. The Court deemed the entire appeal a "fraud on the court" and referred the matter to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for a full investigation into the fabrication of documents and the filing of false proceedings.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the High Court's judgment, which quashed the criminal proceedings against the respondent under Section 482 of the CrPC, should be upheld.
respondent_arguments: The High Court rightly quashed the criminal proceedings in a well-reasoned judgment, holding that even if the entire material collected during the investigation is assumed to be true on its face value, no cognizable offence under Section 376 IPC is made out against the respondent.

After a thorough investigation, the investigating officer had already closed the case against the respondent through a supplementary chargesheet, and the petitioner did not file any protest petition against this closure.

The criminal case was a false one, initiated against the respondent because his testimony was relied upon for convicting another accused, Vikas Yadav, and the respondent had been subjected to continuous threats and pressure.

cases.case_name: Saumya Chaurasia vs. Directorate of Enforcement
cases.principle: The provided text states that the Court relied on an observation from this case, but does not specify what the legal principle or observation was.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: Every party approaching the court is expected to make a full and correct disclosure of material facts. Advocates, as officers of the court, are expected to assist the court fairly and have a duty to diligently verify facts from the record of the case using their legal acumen, a responsibility that cannot be obviated by acting on a client's instructions.
obiter: A very high standard of professionalism and legal acumen is expected from advocates, particularly designated senior advocates in the highest court, so that they may be emulated by advocates in lower courts.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court found that a serious fraud was committed on both the High Court and the Supreme Court. The respondents, their associates, and their advocates forged and fabricated documents to pursue false proceedings in the name of a person without their knowledge, consent, or authority. These actions, which involved taking the courts for a ride and putting the entire justice delivery system at stake, constitute punishable offenses and a fraud on the court. Due to the gravity and seriousness of the case, the court determined that the matter required an investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).
legal_tests_applied: The principle that filing a petition or affidavit containing a misleading or inaccurate statement to achieve an ulterior purpose amounts to an abuse of the process of the court.
The principle that every party approaching the court is expected to make a full and correct disclosure of material facts.
The principle that advocates, as officers of the court, have a duty to assist the court fairly and diligently verify facts from the record of the case.
policy_considerations: The judicial process cannot become an instrument of oppression or abuse, or a means to subvert justice, as the court exercises its jurisdiction only in furtherance of justice.
The interests of justice and public interest coalesce and are very often one and the same.
A very high standard of professionalism and legal acumen is expected from advocates, particularly designated senior advocates, so they may be emulated by other lawyers.

It is a matter of serious concern when advocates, as officers of the Court, actively participate in ill-motivated litigation and assist unscrupulous litigants in misusing and abusing the process of law to achieve ulterior purposes.
